title: Injectivity of the split-at-a-coordinate encoding
statement: Fix $n \ge 1$ and an index $i \in \{0,\dots,n-1\}$, and consider the map that sends a bit-vector $b \colon \{0,\dots,n-1\} \to \{0,1\}$ to the pair of bit-vectors $(u, v)$ obtained by splitting $b$ at coordinate $i$: namely $u(j) = b(j)$ for $j < i$ and $u(j) = 0$ otherwise, while $v(j) = b(j)$ for $j \ge i$ and $v(j) = 0$ otherwise. This map is injective.
hypotheses_covered: i a fixed coordinate in Fin n
replaced: The padded-pair recoding of Alice's one-bit-per-coordinate conditioning is injective.
